rv.q: Ikoko’s script has plenty to say about hashtag campaigns and governments that would rather not know, and the girls’ play-acting gives it a light touch without ever letting you forget it’s real.
But those reservations aside, this play...is without doubt a gut-punch: imaginative, tender, shocking.
JMK winner Ewa Dina directs an astute and affecting production of this drama inspired by Boko Haram’s abduction of the Chibok schoolgirls
If the aim is to raise awareness of these kidnappings, and to point out the lack of resolution, then Girls is a major success.
While GIRLS may struggle to set awards season alight, there is rock solid and meaningful work here...
Not for the fainthearted, and forthright and heartfelt in equal measure.
Girls is a powerful, thought-provoking, and deeply affecting piece of theatre that brings humanity to tragedy beyond the headlines.
Although it does not quite live up to some of the hype surrounding it and could benefit from a little more polish in certain areas, Mean Girls remains a fun and energetic production.
It is not bad, but it isn't brilliant. Eventually, a sense of unfulfillment lurks around.

cn.t: Critics praise Theresa Ikoko's powerful play for finding moments of joy and friendship amid harrowing subject matter, with reviewers highlighting its fierce yet tender portrayal of the Chibok schoolgirls and its ability to balance laughter with profound emotional impact.
